Skeptical economic review — independent first round
29 September 2026. Read-only review of the maintained theoretical paper, Portal accounting, Across
accounting, pool-capacity studies and the existing numerical batch. No main-paper edits, transactions,
privileged calls or state-changing simulations. New arithmetic was evaluated independently with 80-digit
Decimal precision; original experiment identities and outputs were preserved.
Verdict
The narrow conclusion survives: a transferable, valuable source claim can finance a destination
purchase when a funded counterparty accepts it, and a sufficient purchase can raise a
specified market quote. The paper does not establish the significantly stronger original thesis that
validator/admin control and enormous nominal source balances generate that funding, or a self-financing
route to a durable one-dollar pDAI price.
The present conclusion is technically defensible because the hardest economic premises are explicit. Its
vulnerability is informational: assuming destination purchasing liquidity and usable backing can make
the positive result read as “a funded purchase can be funded.” T o become more informative, it needs a
numerical source-to-destination balance-sheet witness and a clear distinction between what the bridge
contributes and where spendable value originates.
What survived independent challenge
Exact token identity, claim conservation, local backing and destination cash are separated correctly.
The source receipt can remain invested while its ownership claim moves, provided the original
holder cannot spend it again.
The report correctly distinguishes a per-trade execution value from a marginal price, and both from
all-holder redemption. The PLS dollar reference is explicitly independent of pDAI.
Portal settlement and ordinary loan repayment are different. The documented accounting
requirement Q >= M + F is correct when proceeds alone fund full backing and F is the actual fee paid.
Current-source documentation is not substituted for the pinned historical implementation.

• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 350

The Portal companion discloses modified-fork tests that left residual unbacked balances instead of
treating a test's “passed” label as full settlement.
Current zero Portal capacity, zero sampled HubPool stable cash and minimal sampled wrapper
output liquidity are disclosed. These contradict an assertion of immediate execution of those exact
routes, not all future configurations.

These are improvements to the interpretation and economic specification, not requests to construct
administrative execution sequences.
Counterexamples to stronger readings
Perfect bridging without value. A source contract escrows one trillion newly issued units and a
destination contract mints exactly matching receipts. All messages and token accounting succeed. There
is no funded bid and no lender accepts the collateral. Destination purchasing power is zero. This
disproves “valid lock/mint plus enormous units implies sufficient buying power.” It does not contradict
the paper's explicit funded-acceptance premise.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 352

Oracle acceptance without new aggregate wealth. A funded lender accepts a receipt at a declared
value and lends its existing PLS. The borrower can spend that PLS. If liquidation cannot recover it, the
lender bears the shortfall. T echnical acceptance can redistribute existing purchasing power even where
collateral is economically weak; it does not establish repeatable solvency. The report should permit this
distinction rather than assume either immediate failure or creation of new economic resources.
Portal at par. Ignore fees and interest. Issue 100 aDAI, sell compatible wrapper claims for 100 pDAI,
and back the full 100. The operator has no remaining pDAI profit; the AMM holds claims of 100 while
Aave holds cash of 100. If the holder redeems those claims, that cash can become market inventory
again. A completed cycle can move liquidity and affect prices, but it neither burns 100 pDAI nor creates
100 free units for repeated intervention. A discount or fee requires additional capital; a genuine premium
may finance a surplus until available pricing opportunities change.
Across inventory exhaustion. Funded relayers deliver 10 million PLS locally and are paid in remote
receipts. If nobody replenishes local PLS, total further local delivery stops after that inventory is spent
even with unlimited remote receipts. This is consistent with healthy bookkeeping and fails the claim of
unlimited destination replenishment from source-unit balances alone.
Competing market. Push one pDAI/PLS pool to one dollar while another deep market offers pDAI
materially cheaper. Funded arbitrageurs can sell into the first pool. A one-pool construction does not
specify the cost of raising the network's executable market, which includes inventory across accessible
venues.
Circular collateral value. Suppose the source receipt ultimately redeems only into the same pDAI
whose one-dollar value the intervention is intended to create. Marking that receipt at the hoped-for
dollar target and borrowing against it assumes the valuation result. Such credit may still be mechanically
available from a funded lender, but its solvency is exposed to the same pDAI decline. Use executable
stressed realization values and identify who bears the loss; do not count an internal oracle mark as an
independent source of support.
PLS repricing. Hold the pDAI/PLS quote fixed while the independent PLS dollar reference halves. pDAI's
dollar-reference execution value halves. PLS-denominated intervention assets and a dollar target are not
a fixed-value reserve system.
Independent arithmetic
Using the paper's inputs x=1,000,000, y=1,000,000,000, s=0.0001, k=xy and T=1, A separate calculation obtained:
Marginal-target input: 2,162,277,660.168379331998893544... PLS.
Subsequent-sale target for q=1,000: 2,167,281,613.012984016139208948... PLS.
That sale returns exactly 10,000,000 PLS within high-precision arithmetic.
After that sale, the resulting marginal dollar-reference price is approximately 0.996842718386987,
illustrating that the successful finite quote does not promise that subsequent trades enjoy the same
price.
Both formulas and supplied numerical results are correct. The assumption of a fee-free pool is explicit, so
absence of fees is not an arithmetic defect. The standard constant-product and marginal-price model is
supported by the Uniswap v2 primary white paper, which also explains that arbitrage links a pool's price
to external markets. No real-world funding conclusion follows from that isolated calculation.

• 
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 353

Useful numerical witness to add
A theoretical balance sheet could stipulate a transferable source claim with independently specified
realization value; escrow it; issue an exclusive representation; have a funded destination buyer pay an
explicit amount of PLS; and apply those PLS to the existing market example. The buyer's PLS must fall by
exactly the purchaser's proceeds and the buyer must acquire the claim. Source investment stays put;
ownership changes. This would establish composition without pretending that the bridge itself creates
the PLS.
A lending variant must add the borrower's liability, lender receivable, liquidation haircut, cash funding
and repayment/rollover assumption. A local stablecoin issuer variant must add the issuer's basket
obligation and the funded market willing to exchange its output. Giving each mechanism an equivalent
complete ledger is more useful than listing additional protocol names.
Falsifiability and open questions
A conditional claim is not falsified by a premise failing in today's deployment. It is weakened if its
premises are mutually inconsistent, rely on the outcome being assumed, or omit a liability that defeats
the claimed budget. Distinguish:
Can an exclusive source claim survive transfer and redemption without double allocation? A
conflicting claim or uncontrolled dilution defeats that model.
What exact spendable asset pays the purchaser, who held it before, and what do they receive? No
funded counterparty defeats that financing instance.
Are all obligations maturing before/during the purchase funded after costs? Check every
chronological prefix, not only the final net balance. A negative intermediate cash balance defeats
the sequence without explicitly funded credit. Cross-chain waiting periods cannot be presumed
atomic; shared reserves cannot be paid out to two routes simultaneously.
What source assets or income ultimately service long-term debt? Unfunded maturity defeats
repeatability even if today's purchase succeeds.
What seller-flow/horizon does the proposed budget cover? Selling beyond that bound defeats the
stated price-support guarantee.
What happens to pDAI purchased for backing when receipt holders redeem or borrowers withdraw
unlocked collateral? These flows can reverse supply removal.
Which independently observed PLS reference defines the target, and what trade size and duration
does “one dollar” describe?
Provisional epistemic judgments
These are broad subjective judgments about support for explicit propositions, not calibrated market
probabilities, frequencies from repeated experiments, or a forecast that any wallet will act. Logical
accounting findings matter more than small numerical differences. reviews share a record and are not
independent samples.

valued and a counterparty is funded
97% 93–99%
H2: The paper establishes a complete
route executable at the pinned
deployed snapshot

nominal copied collateral alone suffice
for the target
1% 0–3%
H4: The paper establishes a durable
one-dollar target under selling and
redemption

H5: The finite AMM existence
calculation is valid under its explicit
assumptions

H2 and H4 ask whether the paper establishes a result. A low score is not the probability that a hidden
system exists or that a future price move occurs. H3 has a direct zero-bid counterexample. The nonzero
ranges acknowledge possible misreading of proposition wording, not a statistical estimate of on-chain
fate.
Round two must challenge these findings after the team's first-round results are shared; this file
preserves the independent first-round review.
